name: Paiwan
notes: Paiwan (pinayuanan), a Formosan language of southern Taiwan and one of the most conservative Austronesian languages. The mapping follows the official Latin orthography promulgated for Taiwan's indigenous languages (2005), with values as given for the Kuljaljau dialect: ⟨tj dj⟩ are the palatal stops /c ɟ/, ⟨dr⟩ the retroflex /ɖ/, ⟨lj⟩ the palatal lateral /ʎ/, ⟨q⟩ the uvular /q/, ⟨c⟩ /ts~tʃ/ and ⟨'⟩ the glottal stop. Four vowels /a ə i u/. Dialects differ considerably; only the standard orthography is modelled.

sources.notes: §1.5 Paiwan orthography (pp. 14-15), read on the page image (the scan has no text layer). Four vowels a e i u with ⟨e⟩ = ə, and 23 consonants in Ferrell's (1982) spelling: p t k q, b d g, m n ng, ts tj dj, s h, v z, l r ł ḍ, w y; ⟨q⟩ is a glottal stop in some dialects and a backed k in others, ⟨ng⟩ = ŋ, ⟨ł⟩ a lateral affricate, ⟨r⟩ a trilled approximant, ⟨ḍ⟩ a retroflex alveolar plosive, and the apostrophe marks a non-phonemic glottal stop in loans only. The comparison table on p. 15 shows the Bible orthography writing ⟨c⟩ for ts and ⟨r l⟩ where Ferrell has ⟨ḍ ł⟩, and Egli using ⟨tj⟩ for both tj and dj. Against this map, which follows the 2005 official spelling: the ⟨lj⟩ and ⟨dr⟩ digraphs correspond to Ferrell's ⟨ł ḍ⟩, and the map's ⟨c⟩ = ts/tʃ key is the Bible spelling, not Ferrell's; the map's ⟨lj⟩ = ʎ is a palatal lateral where the source calls ⟨ł⟩ a lateral affricate. Recorded here, not changed.
